title: What does XChainAddClaimAttestation do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XChainAddClaimAttestation and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, XChainAddClaimAttestation submits a bridge witness's statement about a cross-chain value commitment. [1]

The claim identifier and bridge parameters bind the statement to an intended transfer. Completion depends on the bridge's required attestations and destination state. A source-chain transaction hash alone does not establish that the recipient has received funds. Reconcile both sides before labeling a cross-chain transfer as settled. [1]

The XChainAddClaimAttestation reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using XChainAddClaimAttestation, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
